free_tier.stated: The vendor page offers no amount at all. It advertises 'Azure Research Credits' for 'a proof of concept, migrate existing research workloads and datasets to the cloud, or build tools to facilitate research', and the only route is a contact form whose required fields are 'Email*(Must be a work or school email alias)', 'Institution Name*' and 'Job Role*'. The award, its size and its expiry are all decided after that conversation, so no number exists to record.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: None reachable. Because the amount is negotiated rather than published, there is nothing to compose and nothing to plan against.

limits.value: the entry form rejects a personal address by rule - 'Must be a work or school email alias' - and requires an institution name, so an unaffiliated applicant cannot open the conversation.

'Create a proof of concept, migrate existing research workloads and datasets to the cloud, or build tools to facilitate research with Azure Research Credits', quoted; and 'A member of our team will contact you to continue the process together'

notes: Recorded as the negative half of Azure's academic lane, and specifically because it publishes no number: a reader who hears 'Azure research credits' and finds this page learns only that a conversation exists. The adjacent Azure lanes are worse for a user, not better: AFMR granted 'up to $20,000 in Azure credits' through a university call that closed in January 2024, and the Azure-for-nonprofits grant is USD 2,000 a year but needs nonprofit status. The one Azure program that names individual researchers - AI for Good - is separate in this record and fails on a Washington State condition instead. So all four Azure academic routes close, on three different conditions.
